question: The World Meteorological Organization's (WMO) report, Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update (2025-2029), warns that the Earth’s average temperature may rise by how much above pre-industrial levels?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.2ºC to 1.9ºC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Meteorological Organization's (WMO) report, Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update (2025-2029), highlights that the global average temperature is expected to rise by **1.2ºC to 1.9ºC** above pre-industrial levels.
 
• This projection aligns with the ongoing trend of increasing global temperatures due to **human-induced climate change**, primarily caused by greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The report warns of significant consequences, including **more frequent extreme weather events**, rising sea levels, and ecosystem disruptions.
 
• WMO emphasizes that reaching these temperature thresholds would make it increasingly challenging to achieve the **Paris Agreement goals** of limiting global warming to below 2ºC, preferably 1.5ºC.
 
• The findings serve as a critical call to action for governments to implement **stronger climate mitigation and adaptation strategies** to curb the impact of global warming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The WMO's Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update provides crucial insights into the trajectory of global warming.
 
• It is an essential tool for policymakers to understand climate risks, adapt to changing conditions, and make informed decisions to combat climate change.
 
• Emphasis is placed on reducing **greenhouse gas emissions**, transitioning to renewable energy, and enhancing global cooperation to achieve climate goals.
